Sub-section (1) of section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure provides that a Magistrate shall conclude the trial of a case within 120 days from the date on which the case is received by him for trial and sub-section (3) of the said section 339C Cr. P.C. Provides that, if for any reason a Magistrate is unable to conclude the trial of the case within the specified period of 150 days, he shall conclude the trial within 30 days after the expiry of the aforesaid period of 150 days. In the instant ease it appears from the order sheet that on 16.4.87 the case was received by Mr. Md. Abdul Kuddus, the Additional District Magistrate on transfer for trial as the previous Additional District Magistrate had gone away on transfer. It appears also, that although the previous Additional District Magistrate received this case on 26.2.87 from the District Magistrate, but when he went away on transfer, the District Magistrate withdrew the case to his own file and on 13.4.87 transferred it to Mr. Md. Abdul Kuddits, Additional District Magistrate for disposal. Mr. M.A. Kuddus, Additional District Magistrate, as already, stated, received the case for trial on 16.4.87. On 13.6.87 the District Magistrate again had to withdraw the case to his own file and the District Magistrate transferred the case to Mr. Nasiruddin, Additional Magistrate who received the case on 14.6.87 for trial. Therefore the limitation under section 339C Cr. P.C. in the instant case in the Court of Mr. Nasiruddin, Additional District Magistrate will run from 14.6.87 to 9.11.87 on which date the Sessions Judge, Madaripur stayed the  proceedings in the court of the Additional District. Magistrate Undisputedly from 14.6.87 the limitation upto 11.11.87 has not expired in that Court. Sub-section (1),(3) and (6) of section 339C of the Code provides as follows: 

 The term "Magistrate" includes the District Magistrate and the Additional District Magistrate The aforesaid statutory previsions make it unambiguously clear that the period of limitation of working days for conclusion of trial is in respect of the individual Magistrate who receives the case for trial. The use of the word "him" in the expression "from the date on which the case is received by him for trial." Thus makes it clear that the limitation of working days is in respect of the individual Magistrate who has received the case for trial and this provision of law does not permit the addition of the number of working days of .all the various Magistrate who may have received the case previously for trial. So in the instant case limitation, will not run from 26.2.87 on which date the first, Additional District Magistrate received the case for trial. In respect of the cases sent no the Judges of the Courts of Sessions for trial in calculating the period of limitation for the purpose of releasing the accused petitioners on stopping of the proceedings under section 135C(4).  Therefore, the limitation under section 339C Cr. P.C. shall run afresh from 17.4.88 in the Court Mr. Mohammad All Khan, Additional Sessions Judge, Second Court, Dhaka because sub-section (2) read with subsections (3) and (4) Of section 339C Cr.P.C. provides that, a Sessions Judge, an Additional Sessions Judge or an Assistant Sessions Judge shall conclude the trial of case within 240 (working) days (plus extended time of 30 working days, if necessary) from the date one which the "case is received by hint for trial. So there is no substance whatsoever in the 'argument that the' period of working days front 13.5.87 or 7.6.87 to 15.4.88 of the first trial court of Humayun Ali Additional Sessions Judge is to be added to the working days of the transferee trial Court of. Mr. Mohammad Ali Khan, Additional Sessions Judge from 17.4.88 onwards in the present case in calculating the period of limitation flit.the purpose of releasing the accused stopping the proceedings under section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure." 

 5. The same principle will apply in the successor presiding Judges of a Court, that is fresh limitation will start running, in the Court of successor Judges front the date when he receives the case for trial, that is, When he starts functioning as trial Judge in respect of a particular case. In that view, of the matter, the application is summarily rejected and the order of stay granted by this Court on 26.9.88 is hereby vacated.
